"As enjoyable as the play is, the thunderous ovation at the end of these 2 ½ hours is primarily for the dazzlingly brilliant Janet McTeer. Guided by the savvy director Moritz von Stuelpnagel, the Tony-winning star makes not just a meal but an entire tasting menu out of the central role of the celebrated French actress Sarah Bernhardt.
Director Daniel Sullivan hits just the right tone of contained insanity and arch cynicism.
She's a natural force beneath her leonine pile of gold curls — by turns anxious and imperious, vulnerable and funny and fierce.
As soon as the lights go up and she begins soliloquizing—“Oh what a rogue and peasant slave am I!”—we are immediately, completely, utterly, spellbound.
Regardless of the title, the soul gripping center of this show is Janet McTeer, and what a whirlwind she is.
“Bernhardt/Hamlet” deserves to be seen twice and revived often.

cn.t: McTeer delivers a magnetic, star-making performance as Sarah Bernhardt, but critics find Rebeck's play overwritten and dramatically uneven. The timely feminist themes resonate, though the execution often feels heavy-handed and the narrative meanders.
